the expression of phosphatydylinositol kinase genes in Giardia is essential for growth and encystation.

the identification and characterization of phosphatidylnositol kinase genes in a parasitic protozoa, Giardia.
the identification and analysis of the genes encoding phosphatidylinositide‐kinase in Giardia lamibia.
the identification of the genes that are involved in the regulation of the growth and differentiation processes in G. lambliae.

PIKs are essential for the growth and survival of G. lamblía.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
G. lamblía has the ability to transcribe three putative phosphatidyl-inositol kinase genes that are necessary for parasite growth and encystment.

the three PIK genes of G. lambliawere found to be expressed in non‐ encysting and encystem trophozoites, and that the relative levels of their mRNA were highest in the trophozoites cultured in pre‐ encysting medium containing no bile.

we have identified the expression of three putative phosphatidyl‐inositol kinases (gPI3KA1, gPI3KB, gPI4KA) in G. lambla and have determined the expression of these genes in encysting and non‐encysted trophozoite forms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Giardia lambla, a parasite of the gastrointestinal tract, has three PIKs.
the expression of phosphoinositide kinase genes in the parasite is necessary for growth and differentiation.
the expression of the PIK genes is regulated by the availability of bile salts and that these enzymes are required for the survival of the parasite in vitro.
